CloudHost247 Isc: Cookie Policy Effective Date: August 14, 2025 This Cookie Policy explains how CloudHost247 Isc ("we," "us," "our") uses cookies and similar tracking technologies when you visit our websites, use our services, or interact with our content. By using our website and services, you consent to the use of cookies as described in this policy.

1. What Are Cookies? Cookies are small text files placed on your computer, smartphone, or other device when you visit a website. They help websites function, remember preferences, and understand how visitors use the site.

2. Types of Cookies We Use We use the following categories of cookies: a. Strictly Necessary Cookies These cookies are essential for the operation of our website and services, enabling core functionality such as:

Logging into your account

Managing your hosting services

Processing transactions

Without these cookies, our website and services may not function properly.

b. Performance & Analytics Cookies These cookies collect information about how visitors use our website, such as:

Pages visited

Time spent on each page

Errors encountered

We use this data to improve website performance and user experience.

c. Functional Cookies These cookies remember your preferences and choices, such as:

Language settings

Login details

Customized layouts

This allows us to provide a more personalized experience.

d. Targeting & Advertising Cookies These cookies track your browsing habits to show relevant advertisements on our site or third party platforms. They may be set by us or by advertising partners.

3. Third-Party Cookies

Some cookies on our site are placed by third parties, including:

Analytics providers (e.g., Google Analytics)

Advertising networks

Social media platforms

We do not control third-party cookies and recommend checking their privacy/cookie policies.

4. How We Use Cookies

We use cookies to:

Enable essential website functionality

Monitor and analyze usage for improvements

Save your settings and preferences

Deliver relevant marketing and promotions

Improve overall service performance

5. How to Manage & Disable Cookies

You can control or disable cookies through your browser settings. However, please note that some site features may not work correctly if you disable certain cookies. For instructions, visit:

Chrome: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95647

Firefox: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/enable-and-disable-cookies

Safari: https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/manage-cookies

6. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with a new Effective Date. Continued use of our website after changes means you accept the updated policy. Contact Us If you have questions about our Cookie Policy, please contact: privacy@cloudhost247.com www.cloudhost247.com

7. CloudHost247 Preference Centre

Effective upon publication of the CloudHost247 platform implementation, the Cookie Settings control in the website footer opens a preference centre backed by the CloudHost247 platform.

A strictly necessary, HttpOnly consent cookie (ch247_marketing_consent) stores an opaque choice identifier for up to 180 days. It does not contain your name, email address or browsing history.

Optional analytics and marketing categories are off until you allow them. You can accept all, reject optional categories, save a custom choice, or withdraw consent at any time.

When you allow marketing, the site may load the Meta Pixel and send standard events such as page views, product views, searches, cart actions, checkout steps, registration, contact and verified purchases. Meta may set _fbp and _fbc cookies. Withdrawing consent revokes the Pixel, clears known Meta cookies, reloads the current page and refreshes other open tabs.

Server-side Conversions API events are sent only for consented journeys. Purchase value and currency come from a confirmed payment, not from the browser. The platform sends a hashed opaque session identifier and, where present, Meta click/browser cookies; it does not send your name, email address, password or payment-card details by default.

Consent history is retained for up to 180 days, marketing event activity for up to 90 days, and terminal delivery diagnostics for up to 30 days. Financial records and security audit logs are governed by their own retention rules.

Optional first-party Visitor Intelligence is included in the Analytics choice, not the Marketing choice. It starts only after you allow Analytics and only while the site operator has enabled the feature. It uses a random anonymous visitor/session identifier in browser storage to measure sanitized page paths and a live tab heartbeat; declining or withdrawing Analytics stops collection and deletes visitor records linked to that consent.

Visitor Intelligence does not use browser GPS and does not persist raw IP addresses, full referrer URLs, query strings, form contents, customer email addresses or authentication data. Where a verified network address is available, it is resolved locally for an approximate country/city; only coarse city-level location fields are retained. The default analytics retention period is 90 days and may be configured by the site operator.

You can change your choice at any time through Cookie Settings. Browser-level blocking may still be used, but the preference centre is the site-level control for optional tracking.

documents.description: 1. Overview Backups play a critical role in the management and security of websites, applications, and email services. documents.body:
1. Overview Backups play a critical role in the management and security of websites, applications, and email services. By storing copies of your website files, databases, configurations, and emails in a secure location, you can restore your data in the event of system failure, cyber incidents, accidental deletion, or service disruption. Backup services are not automatically included in all CloudHost247 Isc plans. They may be offered as optional paid features for selected services. It remains your sole responsibility as the customer to maintain regular backups of your data and store them in a secure location separate from your hosting account. Using your hosting account as a backup or storage repository is not permitted. We strongly recommend the use of trusted third-party offsite backup solutions such as CodeGuard, JetBackup, or similar services to ensure additional data protection. Although CloudHost247 Isc may perform periodic backups for certain services, we do not guarantee their availability, completeness, or restoration success. We are not liable for any data loss under any circumstances. Our control panel may provide tools that allow you to manually create, download, and restore backups where applicable. Please note that CloudHost247 Isc does not maintain or control third-party backup systems used by infrastructure partners on a per-server or per-package basis.

2. Shared Hosting CloudHost247 Isc performs automated weekly backups for shared hosting environments. This includes, but is not limited to:

Web Hosting

WordPress Hosting

Node.js Hosting

Python Hosting

Reseller Hosting

Any other shared hosting services provided

Users may also create, download, and restore backups via the hosting control panel, especially when applications are installed using tools like Softaculous. Backup limitations may apply:

A maximum of 5 Softaculous backups OR

Up to 15% of total hosting storage capacity

Excessive or recursive backups ("backups of backups") are not allowed. Customers may request restoration or access to available backups while their hosting account remains active. If the account is suspended due to non-payment, renewal is required before any backup access is granted. For terminated accounts, backups may no longer be available as they are periodically overwritten. If a backup is available, a restoration fee may apply. Restoration requests can be submitted to: billing@cloudhost247isc.com Note: Backup restoration does not replace account renewal fees where applicable. We strongly recommend maintaining independent offsite backups using trusted third-party services.

3. Enterprise Servers Backup services for enterprise infrastructure are optional and may require an additional subscription at the time of purchase or deployment. Once enabled, server backups are typically:

Performed weekly at system level

Stored within the same or designated secure data center

Retained for up to four (4) weeks

Backups older than 30 days are automatically overwritten. Customers are responsible for maintaining external copies of critical or historical data before retention cycles overwrite existing backups. CloudHost247 Isc does not guarantee recovery of any specific state of a server at any time. For Dedicated and Virtual Servers, backup solutions can be configured upon request, including additional storage or secondary backup servers.

Restoration Policy

Full server restoration is available from any of the last four weekly backups (if backup service is active)

Partial restoration is not supported, as backups are system-level snapshots

No backups are created for servers without an active backup subscription

Termination Policy Once an enterprise server is terminated, all associated backups are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered. Customers are responsible for exporting data before termination. Enterprise backup requests: enterprise@cloudhost247isc.com

4. Professional Email & Workspace Email backup availability depends on server retention policies and how email clients are configured. If you use third-party email applications (e.g., Outlook, Thunderbird) configured to delete messages from the server after download, those messages will only exist locally on your device and cannot be restored from CloudHost247 Isc. Backups for Professional Email & Workspace services are maintained at the infrastructure level, and CloudHost247 Isc does not directly control or guarantee their retention beyond system policies. For suspended accounts, backup access requires account renewal. Accounts remain in a suspended state for 20 days before permanent termination, after which all data and backups are permanently deleted.

5. Changes to This Policy CloudHost247 Isc reserves the right to modify, update, or revise this Backup Policy at any time without prior notice. Continued use of our services constitutes acceptance of any changes.

6. Contact Us

For questions or support regarding this policy, please contact: legal@cloudhost247isc.com

documents.body:
Fair Usage Policy The use of CloudHost247 Isc products and services is governed by this Fair Usage Policy. It applies to all hosting plans, including shared hosting, reseller hosting, and WordPress hosting, whether they are advertised with limited or "unlimited" resources such as disk space, bandwidth/data transfer, email accounts, databases, and related server resources worldwide. Our hosting services are designed to remain affordable by allowing multiple customers to share the same server infrastructure. To maintain performance and reliability for all users, each customer must ensure that their usage does not negatively impact other users on the same server. Acceptable Use of Resources All hosting plans are subject to reasonable usage limits. Customers may use allocated resources for legitimate website operations, provided such use remains within normal fair usage standards and complies with our Acceptable Use Policy. Excessive usage of resources such as CPU, RAM, disk I/O, inodes, bandwidth, or email storage that impacts server performance or other customers may result in a warning or requirement to upgrade to a higher plan or a dedicated/cloud hosting solution. Prohibited Activities The following activities are not permitted under this policy:

Using hosting services primarily as a file storage platform (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive equivalents)

Large-scale file archiving unrelated to website functionality

Video or audio streaming services (e.g., YouTube-like platforms)

Customers are encouraged to use third-party storage services for such purposes and embed or link content on their websites where appropriate.

Files uploaded to CloudHost247 Isc hosting must be directly related to and actively used by the website.

Resource Monitoring and Enforcement If a website consumes excessive server resources due to poor optimization, security issues, or unusual traffic, the account owner will be notified once usage approaches or exceeds fair usage thresholds. Customers will be given a reasonable opportunity to resolve the issue, optimize their website, or upgrade their plan. Continued excessive usage that affects server stability or other users may require immediate migration to a virtual or cloud server.

In cases where system stability or security is at risk, CloudHost247 Isc reserves the right to temporarily suspend an account without prior notice. Shared Infrastructure Notice Shared, reseller, and WordPress hosting customers operate on a shared infrastructure where server resources are distributed among multiple users. To ensure consistent performance, any account that negatively impacts server or network stability must either resolve the issue or upgrade to a more suitable hosting environment. This transition is considered a positive step, as it typically indicates growth in website traffic and resource needs, and allows for greater performance, flexibility, and control. Policy Updates CloudHost247 Isc reserves the right to modify or update this Fair Usage Policy at any time. Where significant changes occur, customers will be notified via email or through the client dashboard before the changes take effect. For clarity, the terms "bandwidth" and "data transfer" are used interchangeably within this policy.

This policy outlines how we review and respond to claims of trademark and copyright infringement and how we assist rights holders in protecting their legal interest
documents.body:
Trademark & Copyright Infringement Policy At CloudHost247 Isc, we respect and are committed to protecting intellectual property rights. This policy outlines how we review and respond to claims of trademark and copyright infringement and how we assist rights holders in protecting their legal interests.

Domain Name Dispute Claims This policy applies to disputes involving CloudHost247 Isc products and services, excluding domain name disputes. If you have a concern regarding a registered domain name, you must follow the appropriate dispute resolution procedures:

For general domain disputes, refer to the Uniform Domain Name Dispute Resolution Policy (UDRP). All such claims should be submitted to an ICANN-approved dispute resolution provider.

For .ng domain names, disputes must be directed to the Nigeria Internet Registration Association (NIRA) and resolved in accordance with the NIRA Complaints Policy.

Trademark Claims To report a trademark infringement, the complaining party should send an email to: abuse@cloudhost247isc.com with the subject line: "Trademark Claim"

Your email must include the following:

Full name, address, email address, and phone number of the trademark owner

A copy of the trademark certificate or official acceptance letter

Date the trademark was first used

Description of how the trademark is being infringed

Full details (name, address, email, phone) of the alleged infringer

Evidence showing that the alleged infringer is a CloudHost247 Isc customer

Upon receiving a valid complaint, CloudHost247 Isc will investigate and forward the claim to the accused party. During the investigation, we may temporarily restrict access to or remove the disputed material.

If the claim is valid, we may permanently remove or suspend access to the infringing material or take other appropriate action. If the claim is found invalid, access to the material will be restored. This policy does not override the UDRP or NIRA Complaints Policy, and all parties remain subject to applicable ICANN regulations.

Copyright Claims To submit a copyright infringement complaint, please email: abuse@cloudhost247.com with the subject line: "Copyright Claim"

Your submission must include:

Identification of the copyrighted work being infringed

Proof of copyright registration (if available)

Description or location of the infringing material hosted by a CloudHost247 Isc customer

Full contact details of the copyright owner (name, address, email, phone)

Details of the alleged infringer (name, address, email, phone)

A statement confirming that the use of the material was not authorized by the copyright owner

Upon receipt, CloudHost247 Isc will investigate and notify the alleged infringer. We may temporarily remove or disable access to the disputed content during the review process. If the complaint is valid, we may permanently remove or suspend access to the content. If not, the content will be restored promptly.

Counter Notification Policy If you believe content was removed or disabled due to a mistake or misidentification, you may submit a counter-notification by emailing: abuse@cloudhost247.com

Your counter-notification must include:

Identification of the material removed or disabled and its previous location

A statement under penalty of perjury that the material was removed or disabled by mistake or misidentification

Your full name, address, email address, and phone number

Once received, CloudHost247 Isc will forward your counter-notification to the original complainant. The complainant will then have 10 business days to seek a court order preventing restoration of the material. If no legal action is taken within that period, the material may be restored within 14 business days.

Repeated Infringement Policy CloudHost247 Isc reserves the right to suspend or terminate accounts of users who are repeatedly found to violate intellectual property rights, including copyright and trademark infringement.

Domain Brokerage Terms

documents.body:
Domain Brokerage Terms

CloudHost247 will make commercially reasonable efforts to acquire the requested domain on your behalf through legitimate channels. We do not and cannot guarantee that any acquisition, negotiation, or transfer will succeed. A domain being registered by someone else only means it is unavailable for normal registration — it does not mean the current owner has agreed to sell it, will respond to outreach, or will accept any offer.

2. What the service includes

The Domain Brokerage service includes: researching legitimate acquisition routes for the requested domain, attempting contact with the domain owner or an authorized acquisition channel, negotiating on your behalf according to your instructions, recording offers and counteroffers, coordinating payment through your CloudHost247 account, and tracking the domain transfer until it is verified. CloudHost247 acts as an acquisition intermediary and does not itself sell domains owned by third parties.

3. Your maximum budget

Your maximum acquisition budget is confidential. It is never disclosed to the domain owner, a marketplace, or any provider unless you explicitly authorize that disclosure on your brokerage request. Your broker uses your budget only to guide negotiation on your behalf.

4. Charges are always separate

Every charge is itemized separately before you pay: (a) the domain acquisition price agreed with the owner, (b) the CloudHost247 brokerage fee, (c) any transfer fee, and (d) any payment or escrow provider fee, where an actual payment or escrow provider is used. CloudHost247 never hides fees inside the domain acquisition price. Current fee rules are published in your dashboard before a case is created.

5. Offers, counteroffers and your approval

A seller offer or counteroffer is presented to you for review. You may accept, reject, or counter. No offer is accepted on your behalf automatically unless you have explicitly configured a documented automatic approval rule for your case. Every offer and counteroffer is recorded permanently and is never altered after the fact. Offers may carry an expiration set by the offering party; an expired offer is no longer binding.

6. Payment

When an agreement is reached, CloudHost247 issues an invoice to your CloudHost247 account listing every charge separately. Payment is handled by the existing CloudHost247 payment system and your chosen payment method. A transfer is only authorized after payment is confirmed. CloudHost247 does not claim that funds are held in escrow unless an actual escrow or payment provider is performing that function for your transaction.

7. Transfer requirements and delivery

After agreement and payment, the domain must be transferred to CloudHost247 (or another destination you approve) and verified before the case is completed. Transfers may require an authorization (EPP) code from the current registrar, removal of a transfer lock by the current owner, and compliance with the registry and registrar policies of the relevant TLD, including any transfer waiting periods. A case is marked Completed only after the transfer has actually been verified; the domain is then associated with your CloudHost247 account through the supported registrar/domain architecture, after which you may manage the domain functions your registrar actually supports.

8. Privacy and owner contact limitations

CloudHost247 contacts domain owners only through legitimate channels: public RDAP/WHOIS information where available, registrar-provided contact or forwarding mechanisms, public business contact information, the domain's own public website, and authorized marketplace or broker channels. Where registrant contact details are protected by a registrar privacy service, they are not exposed, and CloudHost247 does not scrape, purchase, or attempt to bypass privacy-protected registrant information. Some owners therefore cannot be reached; this is a recognized limitation of every brokerage service.

9. Third-party provider dependencies

Some acquisition routes depend on third-party marketplaces, brokerage providers, registrars, or payment providers. Those providers have their own terms, availability, fees, transfer policies and processing times. CloudHost247 is not responsible for the actions, availability, or refusals of third-party providers or domain owners. Where no automated provider route exists, a CloudHost247 broker may be assigned to handle your case manually; your dashboard experience is the same either way.

10. Negotiation expiration and inactivity

Offers and counteroffers may expire. If you do not respond to an offer awaiting your approval within the stated period, the offer lapses and may not be repeatable on the same terms. Cases left inactive for an extended period may be closed after notice.

11. Cancellation

You may cancel your brokerage request from your dashboard at any time before an agreement is reached. Once an offer you approved has been accepted and payment has been made, cancellation is subject to the seller's and provider's terms and may no longer be possible.

12. Refund rules

If no agreement is reached, you owe no acquisition price. If a case is cancelled or fails after payment, refundable amounts are returned in accordance with the case agreement, the CloudHost247 Refund Policy, and any non-refundable third-party provider, escrow or transfer fees already incurred, which are always disclosed to you. A refund is never automatic merely because a case slows down; refund outcomes follow the recorded agreement and payment provider rules.

13. Disputes

If you believe something about your case is wrong, contact support promptly and we will review it. A case may be marked Disputed while it is reviewed; during a dispute, irreversible actions (such as transfer completion) are paused. Disputes are resolved case by case against the recorded offer ledger, timeline, and payment records.

14. Your responsibilities

You agree to provide accurate contact information, to set a budget and instructions you can actually honor, to respond to offers in a timely manner, to pay agreed amounts when an agreement is reached, and to cooperate with any transfer requirements. You confirm that your intended use of the domain is lawful and does not infringe third-party rights; CloudHost247 may decline or cancel a brokerage request for a domain that appears intended for trademark abuse or fraud.

15. Changes to these terms

CloudHost247 may update these Domain Brokerage Terms from time to time. The version in force when a brokerage case is created governs that case unless a change is required by law. Material changes are posted to this page with an updated effective date.

Questions

Questions about a brokerage case or these terms can be raised from your CloudHost247 dashboard or with our support team:

documents.body:
Domain Name Auto-Renewal and Deletion Policy Domain Name Auto-Renewal CloudHost247 Isc provides an optional Auto-Renew feature to ensure uninterrupted domain service for all registrants. When enabled, your domain will be automatically renewed using available funds in your account balance or via the credit/debit card you have securely saved in our system. If sufficient funds are not available at the time of renewal, we will notify you via email so you can complete the renewal manually. To help prevent service interruption or domain loss, domain registrations may be set to Auto Renew by default. By using this feature, you authorize CloudHost247 Isc to securely store and charge your selected payment method during domain registration, renewal, or transfer processes.

Auto-renewals are processed for a 1-year extension per cycle.

Renewal charges will be based on the current applicable rates at the time of renewal, which may differ from the original purchase price.

You may disable Auto-Renewal at any time from your account settings.

Domain Name Expiration and Deletion

If payment is not successfully processed on or before the domain renewal date, your domain will expire.

Within 1 day after expiration: The domain may be deactivated and replaced with a parking page indicating expiration. Associated services such as websites or email may stop functioning.

From approximately 36 days after expiration: The domain may become available for registration by third parties. If another party acquires the domain, it can no longer be recovered or renewed by you.

Redemption Period (around 40 days after expiration): If the domain is not purchased by a third party, it may enter the registry redemption period as defined by the domain registry. During this stage, recovery may still be possible, but a redemption fee plus renewal charges will apply. Fees vary depending on the domain extension (TLD).

After redemption period: The domain may be held briefly (typically up to five days) by the registry before being released for general public registration.

documents.description:
Cybercrime Detection Policy

1. Purpose CloudHost247 Isc ("the Company") is committed to ensuring that all domains registered, hosted, or managed on its platform ("the Platform") are not used for illegal, fraudulent, or malicious activities. This policy explains the preventive and detection measures
documents.body:
Cybercrime Detection Policy

1. Purpose CloudHost247 Isc ("the Company") is committed to ensuring that all domains registered, hosted, or managed on its platform ("the Platform") are not used for illegal, fraudulent, or malicious activities. This policy explains the preventive and detection measures used by the Company to identify suspicious or fraudulent domains, as well as the procedures for handling complaints related to cybercrime or abuse involving domains on the Platform. It also outlines how individuals or organizations can report and resolve concerns relating to fraud or other cyber-related offenses involving domains hosted by the Company.

2. Scope This policy applies to:

All employees of CloudHost247 Isc

All visitors and users of the Platform

All registered clients (Registrants)

All complainants and reporting parties

3. Fraudulent Domain Definition

A fraudulent domain refers to any domain name or hosted service that is used to carry out fraud, deception, or any form of cybercrime. This includes, but is not limited to:

Identity theft or impersonation websites

Cyberterrorism-related activities

Forgery or document falsification services

Advance fee fraud schemes

Online financial scams

Domains designed to imitate banks, fintech platforms, or recognized financial institutions

CloudHost247 Isc strictly prohibits the registration or hosting of fraudulent domains. If such domains are detected or reported, they will be immediately suspended or removed following investigation by the Abuse Team.

4. Fraud Prevention and Detection

The CloudHost247 Isc Abuse Team conducts regular monitoring and security reviews of domains hosted on the Platform to identify suspicious or potentially fraudulent activity. When a suspicious domain is identified, the Abuse Team will:

Contact the Registrant for clarification regarding the domain's purpose and associated business activity

Request supporting documentation or verification where necessary

If the Registrant provides valid and verifiable information confirming legitimate use, the domain will remain active. If the Registrant fails to respond within 7 working days, or cannot prove legitimate use of the domain, the Company reserves the right to:

Suspend the domain immediately

Terminate hosting services associated with the domain

5. Complaints and Reporting

If any individual suspects that a domain or service hosted on CloudHost247 Isc is being used for fraudulent or criminal purposes, they should report it via email to: support@cloudhost247.com

Upon receipt of a complaint, the Abuse Team will:

Review and assess the report

Notify the affected Registrant when necessary

Suspend the domain or service if evidence of abuse is found

Registrant contact details will only be disclosed:

When legally required through a valid court order or law enforcement request

CloudHost247 Isc may also, at its discretion, escalate serious cases to relevant law enforcement authorities for further investigation.

6. Contact Information To report abuse, fraud, or suspicious activity involving any domain hosted on CloudHost247 Isc, please contact: Email: support@cloudhost247.com

documents.body:
CloudHost247 Isc: Data Deletion Instructions Effective Date: August 14, 2025 At CloudHost247 Isc, we respect your right to control your personal data. This document provides step-by-step instructions for requesting the deletion of your personal information in compliance with applicable data protection laws, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).

1. Eligibility for Data Deletion You may request deletion of your personal data if:

You no longer use our services.

You withdraw your consent for processing (where applicable).

The data is no longer necessary for the purpose it was collected.

You believe your data has been unlawfully processed.

Certain legal obligations (such as tax, fraud prevention, or dispute resolution requirements) may require us to retain some information temporarily even after a deletion request.

2. What Data Can Be Deleted

We can delete the following:

Account profile details (name, email, contact number)

Billing and payment history (after legal retention periods)

Service usage logs and communications

Stored files, emails, and hosting data associated with your account

We cannot delete data that we are legally required to keep for regulatory or compliance purposes until the retention period expire.

3. How to Request Data Deletion Follow these steps to request deletion:

Step 1 Submit Your Request Send an email to privacy@cloudhost247.com with the subject line: Data Deletion Request. Include:

Full name

Account username or customer ID

Registered email address

A brief statement confirming you wish to have your data deleted

Step 2 Identity Verification

we will verify your identity to protect your account from unauthorized requests. This may involve:

Sending a confirmation code to your registered email address

Requesting a copy of a valid ID (for high-risk requests)

Step 3 Processing Your Request once verified:

We will delete your data within 30 calendar days (or sooner if possible).

You will receive a confirmation email when deletion is complete.

4. Impact of Data Deletion

After your data is deleted:

You will lose access to your account and all services linked to it.

All backups, files, and hosted content will be permanently erased.

The action is irreversible once deleted; we cannot recover your data.

5. Exceptions

We may retain certain information if required to:

Comply with legal obligations

Resolve disputes

Enforce agreements

Maintain necessary business records for accounting, tax, or security purposes

6. Contact Information For any questions or concerns regarding data deletion, contact: privacy@cloudhost247.com www.cloudhost247.com

These Data Protection Standards outline the principles, measures, and responsibilities we follow to ensure comp
documents.body:
CloudHost247 Isc: Data Protection Standards Effective Date: August 14, 2025 At CloudHost247 Isc, safeguarding the personal data of our customers, partners, and employees is a top priority. These Data Protection Standards outline the principles, measures, and responsibilities we follow to ensure compliance with applicable data protection laws, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and other relevant regulations.

1. Purpose The purpose of this policy is to:

Protect personal data from unauthorized access, loss, alteration, or disclosure.

Ensure compliance with all applicable privacy and data protection regulations.

Maintain the trust of our customers, employees, and partners.

2. Scope These standards apply to:

All employees, contractors, and partners of CloudHost247 Isc.

All systems, processes, and technologies used to store, process, or transmit personal data.

All personal data collected through our websites, services, support channels, and business operations.

3. Data Protection Principles

We follow these core principles when handling personal data: 1. Lawfulness, Fairness, and Transparency Data is processed lawfully and transparently. 2. Purpose Limitation Data is collected for specific, legitimate purposes and not processed beyond those purposes. 3. Data Minimization Only the minimum necessary personal data is collected and retained. 4. Accuracy Personal data is kept accurate and up-to-date.

5. Storage Limitation Data is kept only as long as necessary for business or legal purposes. 6. Integrity and Confidentiality Appropriate security measures are implemented to protect data. 7. Accountability We maintain records and proof of compliance.

4. Data Collection and Use

We collect personal data only for purposes related to the provision of our services, customer support, and legal compliance.

Data may include contact details, billing information, technical usage data, and support communications.

Sensitive data is collected only when strictly necessary and with explicit consent.

5. Data Security Measures

To protect data, CloudHost247 Isc implements:

Encryption of data in transit (TLS/SSL) and at rest.

Access controls to limit data access to authorized personnel only.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) for administrative accounts.

Regular security audits and penetration testing.

Firewalls and intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS).

Daily backups stored in secure, encrypted locations.

6. Data Retention

Personal data is retained only for as long as necessary for its intended purpose, in line with our Privacy Policy and legal requirements.

After retention periods expire, data is securely deleted or anonymized.

7. Data Sharing

We only share personal data with trusted third-party service providers, and only when necessary to deliver our services.

All third-party providers must comply with strict contractual data protection obligations.

We do not sell personal data to third parties.

8. Rights of Data Subjects

Under applicable laws, individuals have the right to:

Access their personal data.

Request correction or deletion.

Restrict or object to processing.

Request data portability.

Withdraw consent at any time (where applicable).

Requests can be made by contacting privacy@cloudhost247.com.

9. Incident Response

All data breaches or suspected breaches are reported immediately to our Data Protection Officer (DPO).

We investigate and respond promptly; including notifying affected individuals and authorities when required by law.

10. Employee Responsibilities

All employees handling personal data must follow these standards.

Employees receive regular data protection and cyber security training.

Access to personal data is restricted to those who need it to perform their duties.

11. Compliance and Monitoring

We review and update these standards regularly to ensure compliance with evolving regulations and industry best practices. Internal audits are conducted at least annually.

Contact Us If you have questions about these Data Protection Standards or our data practices, contact:

Data Privacy Notice and Consent Form

1. Introduction CloudHost247 Isc ("we", "our", or "the Company") is committed to protecting the privacy and personal data of all prospective employees in compliance with the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023 and other applicable data protection regulations. This Privacy Notice explains how we collect, use, store, share, and protect your personal data when you apply for employment through our Careers page or any of our recruitment channels. By submitting your application, you confirm that you have read and understood this Notice and consent to the processing of your personal data as described herein.

2. Personal Data We Collect During the recruitment process, we may collect and process the following categories of personal data: a. Identity Information

Full name

Date of birth

Gender (where voluntarily provided)

Photograph (if included in CV)

b. Contact Information

Email address

Phone number

Residential address

c. Professional & Employment Information

Curriculum Vitae (CV)

Cover letter

Employment history

Educational background

Certifications and qualifications

References

LinkedIn or professional profile links

Guarantor's details (name, organization, position, contact information)

Employment verification and reference feedback from previous employers

d. Sensitive Personal Data (if voluntarily provided)

Health information

Disability status (for accommodation purposes)

Background check information (where applicable and legally permitted)

We request that you only provide information relevant to your job application. Where you provide personal data of a guarantor or referee, you confirm that you have informed the individual and obtained their consent for their data to be shared with us for recruitment purposes.

3. Purpose of Processing

We process your personal data for the following lawful purposes:

To assess your suitability for employment

To communicate with you regarding your application

To conduct interviews and recruitment evaluations

To perform background, employment verification, or reference checks (where applicable)

To maintain recruitment records

To comply with legal and regulatory obligations

We do not use your personal data for unrelated purposes without obtaining additional consent where required.

4. Lawful Basis for Processing

In accordance with the NDPA 2023, we rely on the following lawful bases:

Consent - where you voluntarily submit your application

Pre-contractual necessity - processing required before entering into an employment contract

Legal obligation - where required by Nigerian law

Legitimate interest - for recruitment and talent management, provided such interests do not override your fundamental rights

5. Data Sharing and Disclosure

We may share your personal data with:

Internal HR and hiring managers

Background screening providers (where applicable)

IT service providers supporting recruitment systems

Regulatory or law enforcement authorities (where legally required)

We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal data to third parties. Where third parties process data on our behalf, we ensure they are bound by confidentiality and data protection obligations in line with the NDPA.

6. Data Retention If your application is unsuccessful, we may retain your data for 6 - 12 months for future opportunities, unless you request earlier deletion. If your application is successful, your data will form part of your employee record and be retained in accordance with our internal employee data policies. After the retention period, your data will be securely deleted or anonymized.

7. International Data Transfers As a technology and hosting service provider, some of our systems may be hosted outside Nigeria. Where your personal data is transferred internationally, we ensure that:

Adequate safeguards are in place

Transfers comply with NDPA cross-border data protection requirements

8. Data Security

We implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures, including:

Secure servers and encrypted connections (SSL)

Access controls and authentication systems

Confidentiality obligations for staff

Regular monitoring and system security reviews

9. Your Rights Under the NDPA

Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act, you have the right to:

Access your personal data

Request correction of inaccurate data

Request deletion (right to erasure), subject to legal limits

Withdraw consent at any time

Object to processing in certain circumstances

Request restriction of processing

Lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC)

To exercise your rights, contact: dpo@cloudhost247.com

10. Withdrawal of Consent You may withdraw your consent at any time by contacting us. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before consent was withdrawn. However, withdrawing consent during an active recruitment process may limit our ability to continue considering your application.

11. Consent Declaration

By submitting your application through our Careers page or via email, you confirm that:

The information provided is accurate and truthful

You consent to the collection and processing of your personal data for recruitment purposes as described above

You understand your rights under the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023

documents.body:
Catalog API Contract (Phase 3)

This document is the API contract for the catalog/application-façade layer added in Phase 3. It
covers everything under /api/v1/catalog/* (public) and /api/v1/admin/catalog/* (authenticated
admin). Keep this in sync with the code — the source of truth is
cloudhost247-node/src/routes/catalog-public.ts and cloudhost247-node/src/routes/catalog-admin.ts;
this document should never describe behavior the code doesn't actually have.

Architecture

Routes never query the database directly. Public routes only ever read through
src/services/catalog-service.ts, which enforces "only public/active data" and "only published
pricing" as a single, centrally-tested rule. Admin routes read/write through the same
src/db/catalog-*.ts repository functions. This is the seam a later phase's WHMCS-backed adapter
(WHMCS Adapter → Catalog Repository) would slot into without changing routes or DTOs.

Nothing here talks to WHMCS. WHMCS remains the authoritative order/billing system; this catalog is
an independent, currently order-less product/plan/pricing model for this new Node app.

Data model summary

• products — a sellable category (slug, name, description, product_type ∈
  hosting | domain | service, status ∈ draft | active | disabled, visibility ∈
  public | private, display_order).
• product_plans — a plan/tier under a product (slug unique per product, name, description,
  status ∈ draft | active | disabled, billing_model ∈ one_time | recurring,
  display_order).
• plan_pricing — one row per billing period for a plan (billing_period ∈
  one_time | monthly | quarterly | semi_annually | annually, currency, amount, setup_fee,
  effective_status ∈ draft | published). A row can exist with amount = NULL — this is the
  honest "price not configured yet" state. A DB CHECK constraint
  (plan_pricing_published_requires_amount_check, migration 0006) makes it structurally
  impossible to mark a price published without a real amount; the admin API also validates
  this before hitting the database, to return a clean 400 instead of a raw constraint error.
• plan_features — normalized feature rows per plan (name, value, display_order,
  visibility ∈ public | private). Only public features are ever returned by the public API.

"Available" in every public DTO always means: product.status = 'active' (for a product) — never
inferred from plan/pricing contents. A product can be publicly *listed* while still draft
(available: false, "coming soon") — see below — but its plans/pricing are never exposed while
draft.

Public API — /api/v1/catalog/*

No authentication. No internal fields (ids, status, visibility, unpublished pricing, private
features) are ever present in these responses.

GET /api/v1/catalog

Full public catalog — every publicly-visible product (visibility = 'public'), regardless of
status, ordered by display_order.

**Response 200:**

GET /api/v1/catalog/products?type=<hosting|domain|service>

Same as above, optionally filtered by product type.

• type omitted → all public products.
• type present and valid → filtered.
• type present and invalid (not one of the three enum values) → 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. The
  parameter is validated, never silently ignored.

**Response 200:** { "products": [ PublicProductSummary, ... ] }

GET /api/v1/catalog/products/:slug

Detail for one product, plus its plan summaries (no pricing/features — use the /plans endpoint
for that).

• slug must match ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ (lowercase, digits, single hyphens) or 400
  VALIDATION_ERROR.
• Slug well-formed but no matching *public* product (doesn't exist, or is visibility = 'private')
  → 404 NOT_FOUND. A private product and a genuinely missing slug are **intentionally
  indistinguishable** from the outside — the public API never reveals that a private product
  exists.
• Product exists and is public but status != 'active' (draft) → 200, available: false,
  plans: []. A draft-but-public product is listed as "coming soon", never as an error and never
  with fabricated/partial plan data.
• Product exists, public, status = 'active' → 200, available: true, plans populated with
  PublicPlanSummary entries for that product's active plans.

**Response 200:** { "product": PublicProductDetail }

GET /api/v1/catalog/products/:slug/plans

Full plan detail (pricing + features) for one product.

• Same slug validation/404 rules as above.
• Draft-but-public product → 200, { "product": {...}, "plans": [] } (no partial data leak).
• Active product → 200, plans is an array of PublicPlan, one per **active** plan under that
  product. Each plan's pricing array contains only rows with effective_status = 'published'
  (never a draft/no-amount row); each plan's features array contains only
  visibility = 'public' features. A plan can legitimately have pricing: [] if nothing has been
  published for it yet — this is shown as-is, never substituted with an invented price.

**Response 200:** { "product": PublicProductSummary, "plans": [ PublicPlan, ... ] }

Public DTOs (TypeScript, src/dto/catalog.ts / mirrored in
cloudhost247-node/frontend/src/lib/catalog-types.ts)

Error shape (all endpoints, public and admin)

| HTTP status | error code (typical) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | VALIDATION_ERROR | Malformed/invalid input (bad enum, bad UUID, bad slug shape, business-rule violation e.g. publishing with no amount) |
| 401 | UNAUTHORIZED | Missing/invalid/expired/revoked JWT (admin routes only) |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | Authenticated but not super_admin (admin routes only) |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | No such public product/plan/pricing/feature row, or admin row by id |
| 429 | RATE_LIMITED | Rate limit exceeded (global Fastify rate-limit plugin, unchanged from Phase 2) |
| 500 | INTERNAL_ERROR | Unexpected server error |

Admin API — /api/v1/admin/catalog/*

**Authentication:** Authorization: Bearer <JWT>, required on every route. Uses the same
JWT/jti-revocation model as Phase 2 (src/lib/require-auth.ts) — a token that has been logged
out via /api/auth/logout is rejected here too.

**Authorization:** requireRole('super_admin') (src/lib/require-role.ts). Catalog
administration is restricted to super_admin only — a plain admin role is **not** sufficient
(defense in depth: catalog mutation is treated as a highly sensitive operation). The role is
always read from the server-verified JWT claims, never trusted from any client-supplied value.

All mutations are persisted to PostgreSQL through the repository layer
(src/db/catalog-products.ts, catalog-plans.ts, catalog-pricing.ts, catalog-features.ts) —
there is no React-state-only "fake" admin UI; every create/update call here is a real INSERT/
UPDATE and is asserted to have happened via a follow-up read in
tests/integration/catalog-admin-api.test.ts.

Products

| Method & path | Body | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/v1/admin/catalog/products | – | Full admin product list — includes draft/disabled/private products, unlike the public list. |
| POST /api/v1/admin/catalog/products | { slug, name, description?, productType, status?, visibility?, displayOrder? } | Creates a product. slug must be unique. |
| GET /api/v1/admin/catalog/products/:id | – | Full detail for one product **by UUID**, including its draft plans, unpublished pricing, and private features — i.e. everything the public API deliberately hides. :id must be a valid UUID (400 otherwise); unknown id → 404. |
| PATCH /api/v1/admin/catalog/products/:id | Any subset of { name, description, productType, visibility, displayOrder } | Partial update; only supplied fields change; updated_at always bumps. |
| POST /api/v1/admin/catalog/products/:id/status | { status: 'draft' \| 'active' \| 'disabled' } | Enable/disable a product. Setting disabled (or leaving draft) removes it from the public catalog **immediately** — verified in catalog-admin-api.test.ts by reading the public endpoint right after. |

Plans

| Method & path | Body | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/v1/admin/catalog/products/:id/plans | { slug, name, description?, billingModel, status?, displayOrder? } | Creates a plan under product :id. slug unique per product. 404 if the product id doesn't exist. |
| PATCH /api/v1/admin/catalog/plans/:id | Any subset of { name, description, billingModel, displayOrder } | Partial update. |
| POST /api/v1/admin/catalog/plans/:id/status | { status: 'draft' \| 'active' \| 'disabled' } | Enable/disable a plan; a disabled/draft plan is excluded from listActivePlansForProduct and therefore from every public response, immediately. |

Pricing

| Method & path | Body | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/v1/admin/catalog/plans/:id/pricing | { billingPeriod, currency, amount?, setupFee?, effectiveStatus? } | Creates a pricing row for plan :id. If effectiveStatus: 'published' is requested with no amount, rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR **before** touching the database (the DB CHECK constraint is a second, independent line of defense, not the primary UX). |
| GET /api/v1/admin/catalog/pricing/:id | – | Full pricing row by id, including draft rows and amount: null. |
| PATCH /api/v1/admin/catalog/pricing/:id | Any subset of { currency, amount, setupFee, effectiveStatus } | Partial update. If the resulting row (existing amount, or the amount in this same patch) would be published with no amount, rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Publishing an amount and setting effectiveStatus: 'published' in the **same** request is supported and succeeds. |

Features

| Method & path | Body | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PUT /api/v1/admin/catalog/plans/:id/features | { features: [{ name, value?, displayOrder?, visibility? }, ...] } | Replaces the full feature set for plan :id in one call (delete + re-insert, transactional). visibility defaults to public; set private for internal-only notes that must never reach the public API. |

All :id params above are validated as UUIDs (400 VALIDATION_ERROR on malformed input, distinct
from 404 for a well-formed-but-nonexistent id).

Security notes

• Public endpoints are read-only and return no internal identifiers, no draft/disabled/
  private rows, and no unpublished pricing/private features, under any query parameter
  combination — enforced by the repository-level filtering in src/services/catalog-service.ts,
  not by route-level post-filtering.
• Admin endpoints require both authentication (require-auth.ts) and authorization
  (requireRole('super_admin')) independently; either failing returns the appropriate 401/403
  and takes no action. Every admin mutation test in tests/integration/catalog-admin-api.test.ts
  is proven by reading the row back from the database or from the public API afterward — not just
  asserting a 200.
• No endpoint here performs a WHMCS table passthrough; there is no direct WHMCS DB
  connection/credential anywhere in this code path.

What Phase 3 explicitly does not include

No order, cart, checkout, payment, invoice, or service-activation/provisioning endpoints exist
anywhere in this API. Pricing shown here is informational catalog pricing only; no endpoint in this
document creates a purchase, charges a payment method, or activates a service. That is explicitly
deferred to a future phase.

documents.description: This document is the API contract for Phase 5A, "Commerce foundation": a customer's cart and the orders it becomes when checked out. Keep this in sync with the code - the source of truth is cloudhost2
documents.body:
Commerce API Contract (Phase 5A)

This document is the API contract for Phase 5A, "Commerce foundation": a customer's cart and the
orders it becomes when checked out. Keep this in sync with the code — the source of truth is
cloudhost247-node/src/routes/commerce.ts, cloudhost247-node/src/services/commerce-service.ts,
and cloudhost247-node/database/migrations/0014–0017; this document should never describe
behavior the code doesn't actually have.

Explicit non-goals (this phase)

• **No payment gateway, no payment record, no invoice, no billing ledger yet.** Every order this
  phase creates has status: 'pending' and payment_status: 'unpaid' and nothing in the codebase
  can currently change that — there is no route, job, or webhook that marks an order paid. Those
  land in Phase 5B (billing/invoices/ledger) and 5C/5D (payment gateway + webhooks).
• **No tax or discount configuration system yet.** discount_amount and tax_amount are always
  "0.00" on every order — a genuine zero, not a hidden or placeholder value. A future phase must
  add real tax/discount configuration before these become non-zero for any order.
• **No admin/staff order-viewing routes yet.** Deferred to Phase 5F. Nothing in this phase lets
  staff see, search, or act on another customer's cart or order.
• **No multi-currency support.** Every price, cart, and order in this phase is in a single
  platform-wide currency (see src/config/billing.ts's DEFAULT_CURRENCY, currently USD). No
  request body field can ever change what currency is used.
• Nothing in this layer talks to cPanel/WHM, a domain registrar, or a payment provider. Placing an
  order records a purchase intent — it does not provision, activate, or configure anything.

Architecture

Every response is built only through src/dto/commerce.ts — the same "never leak an internal
field, never fabricate a price" mapping-layer pattern used by the Phase 3 catalog DTOs
(src/dto/catalog.ts) and Phase 4 account DTOs (src/dto/account.ts).

Data model summary

• carts (0014) — exactly one cart per customer, enforced by a unique index on user_id.
  Created lazily (get-or-create) the first time a customer touches their cart; has no financial
  significance of its own.
• cart_items (0015) — a cart line references only plan_id (never a separate product_id —
  the product is always reached via product_plans.product_id, so it can never drift out of sync)
  plus a billing_period. No price is stored on a cart line; it is always resolved live from
  plan_pricing at read/checkout time. Unique on (cart_id, plan_id, billing_period) — adding the
  same plan+cadence again increases quantity instead of duplicating the line. quantity is capped
  at 20 per line (cart_items_quantity_positive_check).
• orders (0016) — the first genuinely financial table in the platform. order_number is
  generated by the database itself from a dedicated order_number_seq sequence
  ('CH-' || lpad(nextval(...)::text, 8, '0')) — atomic and race-free under concurrent checkouts,
  never client-supplied, never app-generated. user_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT (not CASCADE):
  a user with order history can never be deleted out from under it. status (pending /
  completed / cancelled / failed) and payment_status (unpaid / pending / paid /
  failed / refunded / partially_refunded) are separate columns — Phase 5A only ever produces
  pending / unpaid.
• order_items (0017) — an immutable price **snapshot** per line: product_name_snapshot,
  plan_name_snapshot, unit_price_amount, currency, and line_total_amount are copied at
  checkout time and never recalculated or updated afterward. product_id/plan_id are optional,
  best-effort soft links back to the live catalog (ON DELETE SET NULL) — a later catalog rename,
  price change, or deletion can never alter what a historical order says the customer agreed to
  pay. Every order display reads the *_snapshot columns, never the live catalog.

Money handling

Every monetary DB column is Postgres numeric, which pg/pglite both return as a **string**
(e.g. "19.99") specifically to avoid binary floating-point rounding. src/lib/money.ts is the
one place that converts a monetary string to a number, and always as a whole integer number of
cents — toCents/fromCents/multiplyCents/sumCents. No monetary arithmetic anywhere in the
commerce layer uses native JS +/-/* on a decimal string or float directly.

Transactional integrity

src/db/transaction.ts exports withTransaction(pool, fn), used by checkoutCart to make the
price re-check, the orders/order_items insert, and clearing the cart happen atomically — either
all of it commits, or (on any thrown error, including "cart is empty" or "item no longer
available") none of it does, and the customer's cart is left untouched. This closes a
check-then-act gap between reading a price and writing the order: two requests, or a catalog change
racing a checkout, can never produce a half-written order or an order priced from stale data.

In production, withTransaction checks out one dedicated pg.Pool client via .connect() and
runs BEGIN/the callback/COMMIT-or-ROLLBACK on that same client — calling pool.query('BEGIN')
followed by further pool.query() calls would **not** be a real transaction, because
pg.Pool.query() may use a different underlying connection per call. In tests, it uses
@electric-sql/pglite's native .transaction() API instead.

Authorization model

Every route calls authenticate() (re-verified against the database on every request, same as
Phase 4) and scopes every query to the caller's own user_id. A cart item or order that exists but
belongs to a different customer is never distinguishable from one that doesn't exist at all — both
return 404, never 403.

| Capability | customer | admin | super_admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| View/modify own cart | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) |
| Check out own cart into an order | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) |
| View own order history/detail | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) |
| View/modify another customer's cart or orders | ❌ | ❌ (deferred to 5F) | ❌ (deferred to 5F) |

Price integrity rules (enforced in src/services/commerce-service.ts)

• **No request body ever carries a price, subtotal, tax, discount, total, or currency.** The only
  thing a client can specify is *what* it wants: planId + billingPeriod + quantity. Any such
  field present in a request body is silently ignored (zod schemas for these routes don't even
  define them), never validated against or trusted.
• Adding an item to the cart requires, at that moment: the plan status = 'active', its parent
  product status = 'active' AND visibility = 'public', and a plan_pricing row for that exact
  (plan_id, billing_period, DEFAULT_CURRENCY) with effective_status = 'published'. Any failure
  is a 404 (plan/product not purchasable) or 400 (no published price for that cadence) —
  the same "don't add a line that could never check out" rule applies to checkoutCart, which
  re-validates all of this fresh (not from cached cart-add-time data) inside the transaction.
• GET /api/v1/cart never hides a broken line — priceUnavailable: true and
  hasUnavailableItems: true surface honestly so the customer can remove/resolve it; an
  unavailable line is excluded from subtotalAmount (there is no valid price to add).
• POST /api/v1/orders refuses outright (with a 400 listing the affected plan names) if the cart
  is empty or any line is unavailable — no partial order is ever created.

Endpoints

All endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> and return 401 if missing/invalid.

GET /api/v1/cart

Returns the caller's own cart, creating it on first use.

POST /api/v1/cart/items

Body: { "planId": "<uuid>", "billingPeriod": "one_time"|"monthly"|"quarterly"|"semi_annually"|"annually", "quantity"?: 1-20 (default 1) }.
Upserts — adding a plan/cadence already in the cart increases its quantity. Returns 201 with the
updated cart summary (same shape as GET /api/v1/cart). 404 if the plan doesn't exist or isn't
currently purchasable; 400 if no published price exists for the requested cadence, or the body
fails validation.

PATCH /api/v1/cart/items/:id

Body: { "quantity": 1-20 }. Ownership-checked (404 if the item doesn't exist or isn't the
caller's). Returns the updated cart summary.

DELETE /api/v1/cart/items/:id

Ownership-checked removal. Returns the updated cart summary.

POST /api/v1/orders

Checks out the caller's current cart. No request body is accepted or needed — currency is always
the platform default, prices are always re-read fresh inside one transaction. Returns 201 with
the created order (including its snapshot line items); 400 if the cart is empty or any line is no
longer available (nothing is created in that case).

GET /api/v1/orders

Lists the caller's own orders (summaries, no line items), newest first.

GET /api/v1/orders/:id

Full order detail including line items. Ownership-checked (404, not 403, for another
customer's order — same as every other ownership check in this codebase).

What's next (later Phase 5 sub-phases)

• **5B** — real invoices, a billing ledger (charges/payments/refunds/credits), and payment
  records, built on top of these orders.
• **5C** — a payment gateway abstraction (manual/offline + a self-contained sandbox gateway with
  simulated signed webhooks), checkout initiation.
• **5D** — signature-verified, idempotent, replay-protected webhooks that are the *only* way an
  order's payment_status can ever become paid.
• **5E/5F** — customer-facing billing UI and admin/staff billing management + audit trail.
• **5G** — SMTP notifications (order confirmation, invoice, payment) and reconciliation jobs.

documents.description: This document is the API contract for Phase 5B, "Billing foundation": real invoices, issued automatically and atomically when an order is checked out (Phase 5A), and the append-only billing ledger beh
documents.body:
Billing API Contract (Phase 5B)

This document is the API contract for Phase 5B, "Billing foundation": real invoices, issued
automatically and atomically when an order is checked out (Phase 5A), and the append-only billing
ledger behind them. Keep this in sync with the code — the source of truth is
cloudhost247-node/src/routes/billing.ts, cloudhost247-node/src/services/billing-service.ts, and
cloudhost247-node/database/migrations/0018–0020; this document should never describe behavior
the code doesn't actually have.

See docs/API_COMMERCE.md for the cart/order layer this builds directly on top of.

Explicit non-goals (this phase)

• **Update (Phase 5C):** Payments are no longer schema-only — see docs/API_PAYMENTS.md for the
• full payment gateway/initiation/manual-confirmation contract now built on top of this phase's
• payments table. The invoice detail response below now also includes a payments array. The
• non-goals below describe Phase 5B's own scope at the time it shipped and are left as written for
• history; nothing below is contradicted by 5C, which only *adds* to this table, never edits it.

• **No payment gateway, no way to create or mutate a payment, and no way for any invoice to become
  paid, as of Phase 5B itself.** database/migrations/0020_create_payments.sql adds the
  payments table schema and src/db/payments.ts adds its repository functions, but at the time
  Phase 5B shipped, no route or service anywhere called them. Phase 5C (see docs/API_PAYMENTS.md)
  is what now calls them, through a gateway abstraction, a manual/offline gateway, and a
  self-contained sandbox gateway. Every invoice still starts at status: 'unpaid', and Phase 5C's
  sandbox gateway still cannot move a payment to any terminal state — only Phase 5D's webhook
  receiver, or a staff member confirming a manual payment, can.
• **No tax or discount configuration system yet.** Exactly like orders (Phase 5A), an invoice's
  discount_amount/tax_amount are always "0.00" — a genuine zero, copied verbatim from the
  order, never fabricated.
• **No admin/staff invoice-viewing routes yet.** Deferred to Phase 5F, same as Phase 5A's
  order-viewing routes.
• **No customer billing UI wiring yet** (the /billing//invoices frontend pages) — that's Phase
  5E. This phase is backend-only, per the locked "checkpoint after every sub-phase" cadence.
• Still single-currency (USD), still no cPanel/WHM/registrar automation of any kind.

Architecture

Every response is built only through src/dto/billing.ts — the same "never leak an internal field,
never fabricate a value" mapping-layer pattern used throughout this codebase.

Data model summary

• invoices (0018) — the formal billing document for an order. **One invoice per order** in
  this phase (order_id is UNIQUE) — there is no recurring/subscription billing yet.
  invoice_number is generated by the database itself from a dedicated invoice_number_seq
  sequence ('INV-' || lpad(nextval(...)::text, 8, '0')), the same proven, race-free pattern as
  orders.order_number (Phase 5A) — never client- or app-supplied.
  subtotal_amount/discount_amount/tax_amount/total_amount/currency are a **snapshot**
  copied from the order at the moment the invoice is issued, not a live join — an invoice is its
  own billing record. due_date defaults to the issue date (due on receipt) — there is no
  payment-terms configuration system yet, and this migration does not invent one. status starts
  at unpaid; its full lifecycle (unpaid / paid / void / refunded / partially_refunded)
  exists in the schema now so Phase 5D's verified-webhook processing can use it later, but no code
  in this phase ever sets it to anything else. order_id/user_id are both ON DELETE RESTRICT —
  a customer or order with an invoice can never be deleted out from under it.
• billing_ledger (0019) — the append-only, immutable financial audit trail the Phase 5 spec
  calls for explicitly. Every row is one financial fact: charge (an invoice was issued — the
  only entry type any code creates as of Phase 5B), payment, refund, or credit (all reserved
  for later phases). amount is always a positive magnitude; the accounting direction is implied
  entirely by entry_type. **This table is enforced insert-only at the database level, not just by
  application discipline**: BEFORE UPDATE/BEFORE DELETE triggers make any mutation attempt fail
  outright — including from a future bug, a manual psql session, or a compromised admin route —
  proven directly in tests/integration/billing-schema.test.ts (a raw SQL UPDATE/DELETE
  against the table, and the same attempted inside a transaction, both rejected with the row
  unchanged). Correcting a mistake always means inserting a new, reversing entry — never editing or
  removing the original.
• payments (0020, extended by 0021 in Phase 5C — see docs/API_PAYMENTS.md). Models the
  real payment lifecycle the Phase 5 spec calls for (pending / successful / failed /
  cancelled / expired / refunded / partially_refunded). A partial unique index on
  (provider, provider_reference) (enforced only when both are present) is already in place —
  the exact idempotency guarantee Phase 5D's webhook handling will depend on, so the same verified
  webhook event replayed twice can never create two payment records.

Checkout now issues a real invoice atomically (extends Phase 5A)

checkoutCart (src/services/commerce-service.ts) now also calls
issueInvoiceForOrder (src/services/billing-service.ts) **inside the same withTransaction call**
as the order/order_items insert and the cart clear. The order, its items, its invoice, and that
invoice's opening charge ledger entry are one atomic unit — a checkout can never produce any
strict subset of the four (proven by the existing Phase 5A "reject an empty/unavailable cart, zero
orders created" tests, which now also implicitly prove zero invoices/ledger entries are created).
POST /api/v1/orders's response now includes invoiceId/invoiceNumber directly on the order, and
GET /api/v1/orders / GET /api/v1/orders/:id include the same fields for every existing order.

Authorization model

Identical pattern to Phase 5A/4: authenticate() on every request, every query scoped to the
caller's own user_id. An invoice that exists but belongs to a different customer is never
distinguishable from one that doesn't exist — both 404, never 403.

| Capability | customer | admin | super_admin |
|---|---|---|---|
| View own invoices/ledger detail | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) | ✅ (self only) |
| Create, edit, or void any invoice | ❌ | ❌ (deferred to 5F) | ❌ (deferred to 5F) |
| View another customer's invoice | ❌ | ❌ (deferred to 5F) | ❌ (deferred to 5F) |

There is no POST/PATCH/DELETE route for invoices anywhere — an invoice is only ever produced
as a side effect of checkout, never directly created or edited by any request.

Endpoints

All endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> and return 401 if missing/invalid.

GET /api/v1/invoices

Lists the caller's own invoices (summaries), newest first.

GET /api/v1/invoices/:id

Full invoice detail: the invoice fields above, plus items (the underlying order's line-item
snapshots — see docs/API_COMMERCE.md), ledger (every billing_ledger entry recorded against
this invoice, oldest first), and — as of Phase 5C — payments (every payment *attempt* recorded
against this invoice, oldest first, including cancelled/failed ones; see docs/API_PAYMENTS.md).
Ownership-checked (404, not 403, for another customer's invoice).

What's next (later Phase 5 sub-phases)

• **5C — done, see docs/API_PAYMENTS.md.** The payment gateway abstraction, a manual/offline
  gateway, and a self-contained sandbox gateway; checkout initiation now populates the payments
  table this phase left ready but unused. Deliberately stops at *initiation* — resolving a payment
  is either a staff member confirming a manual one, or Phase 5D's webhook receiver.
• **5D** — signature-verified, idempotent, replay-protected webhooks — the *only automated* way an
  invoice's status or an order's payment_status can become paid (alongside 5C's manual-gateway
  staff-confirmation path, which is a direct human assertion, not an automated one).
• **5E/5F** — customer-facing billing UI (/billing, /invoices) and the broader admin/staff
  billing dashboard (search/filter/view-all-invoices, refunds) + audit trail. (5C added two narrow
  admin endpoints for manual-payment confirm/reject only — see docs/API_PAYMENTS.md.)
• **5G** — SMTP notifications (order confirmation, invoice, payment) and reconciliation jobs.
